commentary.text:
Red takes an early central foothold while preserving open lanes for Yellow to reinforce the other center squares. The piece is not immediately capturable by a sandwich, and this move forces the opponent to contest rather than develop freely.
```memo
### Position read
Opening position except Red now occupies center (3,3). All losses are 0. The central piece is exposed but currently has no immediate same-color opposing sandwich geometry against it.
### Our plan
Use Yellow to reinforce or occupy another center square while Red develops same-color support along useful rows/columns. Contest center actively, but scan opponent landings that could create same-color flanks. Seek captures before committing all four center squares.
### Opponent tendencies
No opponent move observed yet. Expect Blue or Green to contest a center square or stage a rook-line attack on the advanced Red.
### Lessons
Sandwiches require matching colors at both ends; our two colors support space together but cannot flank together. Moving into apparent sandwich geometry is safe because only the mover triggers captures.
```
I’m taking a central foothold on (4,4), where Blue is not immediately sandwiched and can contest Team A’s early center push.

I’m placing Yellow beside the Blue center piece. This secures a second central square for us and creates a same-color Yellow flanking threat: if Blue stays on (4,4), Yellow can later land on (4,5) and capture it.
```memo
### Position read
We hold center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; the opponent holds (4,4) with Blue, while (3,4) is empty. All losses remain 0. Yellow at (4,3) is safe from an immediate Green capture.
### Our plan
Develop Red toward (3,4) if tactically safe. Yellow’s placement threatens a future same-color sandwich by landing at (4,5) while Blue remains at (4,4), likely forcing that Blue piece to retreat. Continue scanning center occupants for rook-line flanks before every commitment.
### Opponent tendencies
Blue contested the center immediately with (4,4). Expect Green to develop toward center or interfere with our support, and expect Blue to move its central piece if the Yellow sandwich threat persists.
### Lessons
A supported geometric threat can gain center tempo even when the capture is not immediate. Keep separate same-color flank plans while using both colors jointly for center occupation.
```
I’m placing a Green anchor below the two central enemy pieces. This threatens a future move to (2,3) that would sandwich both Yellow and Red, forcing Team A to break its central formation.

I’m staging Red at (2,5), keeping both center plans alive. If Blue shifts from (4,4) to (3,4), Red can land at (3,5) and sandwich it against Red at (3,3). If Blue retreats elsewhere, Yellow can occupy (4,4), leaving Red at (0,4) poised to challenge the final center square.
```memo
### Position read
We hold center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; Blue holds (4,4), and (3,4) is empty. Losses are all 0. Red is now staged at (2,5), while Red at (0,4) retains a route toward (3,4).
### Our plan
Blue at (4,4) is threatened by Yellow landing at (4,5), flanking it against Yellow (4,3). If Blue retreats to (3,4), answer on Red’s next turn with (2,5)→(3,5), sandwiching it against Red (3,3); Green cannot readily occupy that landing square. If Blue retreats elsewhere, consider Yellow (7,4)→(4,4) to claim a third center, while watching for Green blocking Red’s column-4 route.
### Opponent tendencies
Blue contests center directly; Green develops pieces to interfere with support and may block key approach lanes rather than attack immediately.
### Lessons
Stage a flank so the capturing move remains available after an opponent enters the line; a pre-existing sandwich does not capture. Preserve multiple center-entry routes and account for Green’s intervening tempo.
```

I tighten the line against the advanced Red piece on row 2. This preserves Blue’s central anchor while threatening to build a same-color sandwich, forcing Team A to respond instead of freely consolidating the center.

Yellow executes the prepared flank, removing Blue’s central piece while keeping our two center occupants secure. This clears (4,4) for a later Yellow entry and maintains Red’s route toward (3,4).
```memo
### Position read
We hold (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow. Yellow moved (7,5)→(4,5), sandwiching and capturing Blue at (4,4) against Yellow (4,3); Blue now has 1 loss. The other center squares are empty. Red remains staged at (2,5), with Red (0,4) potentially entering (3,4). Blue at (2,6) is beside Red (2,5), but currently lacks a distinct Blue mover that can complete that sandwich.
### Our plan
Pursue center occupation through Red (0,4)→(3,4) and Yellow (7,4)→(4,4), adapting if Green blocks one route. Preserve Yellow (4,5) as support and look for another Blue capture to push its losses toward elimination. Check whether Green’s next move creates a capture or blocks columns 4–5 before committing.
### Opponent tendencies
Blue contests the center and has now shifted toward our staged Red piece. Green favors lane-blocking and interference with center-entry routes.
### Lessons
Prepared same-color flanks convert center contests into captures. After taking an intruder, use the cleared square promptly but keep alternative entry routes because Green has an intervening tempo.
```

I’m blocking Red’s direct route down column 4 into the center. This also develops Green close to the central squares and forces Team A to spend time or dislodge it before completing center occupation.

I’m clearing Green’s blocker from column 4. Red lands at (2,3), sandwiching the Green piece at (2,4) against Red at (2,5); this also opens Red’s route toward (3,4) while preserving a piece that can later return to (3,3).
```memo
### Position read
Red moved (3,3)→(2,3), sandwiching Green at (2,4) against Red (2,5); Green should now have 1 loss. We temporarily vacated center (3,3), while Yellow still holds (4,3) and supports from (4,5). Clearing (2,4) opens Red (0,4)'s route to (3,4). Blue has 1 loss and remains at (2,6), adjacent to Red (2,5), but lacks an immediate Blue mover able to land at (2,4).
### Our plan
If safe, play Yellow (7,4)→(4,4), then use Red (0,4)→(3,4) and later Red (2,3)→(3,3) to complete the center. Adapt immediately if Blue or Green occupies or attacks those squares. Seek Blue captures when available because Blue already has 1 loss.
### Opponent tendencies
Blue contests central lanes and pressures staged pieces. Green uses blockers to interrupt center-entry routes.
### Lessons
Removing the column-4 blocker required temporarily vacating a center square, but the capturing Red remains positioned to restore it. Recheck the Blue flank around Red (2,5) after every opponent move.
```
I’m claiming a central square with Blue while leaving (3,3) accessible to Green, creating an immediate center-occupation threat that Yellow must answer.

Yellow steps into (3,3), safely reclaiming a central square while creating a same-color sandwich threat: if Blue remains at (3,4), Yellow can land at (3,5) next turn and capture it against this new flank.
```memo
### Position read
Blue occupied center (3,4). Yellow now holds (3,3), with Yellow (4,5) poised to land at (3,5) and sandwich that Blue against (3,3). Green cannot immediately capture the new Yellow, and Blue has no second piece able to complete a sandwich around it. Losses: opponent Blue 1, Green 1; we have 0.
### Our plan
If Blue stays at (3,4), play Yellow (4,5)→(3,5) next Yellow turn to capture it. Expect Blue to retreat, then preserve (3,3), stage Yellow toward (4,4), and use Red to contest (3,4)/(4,3). Continue targeting Blue because another capture puts it at 2 losses.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests central lanes directly and uses blockers to delay our center formation. Blue will likely evacuate (3,4) now that it is between a prepared Yellow pair.
### Lessons
Building same-color flanks can force a center defender to retreat even before the capture. Recheck any Yellow move into (4,4), since Blue at (3,4) plus a Blue landing at (5,4) could sandwich it.
```
I’m reinforcing Blue’s central foothold by bringing Green into (4,4), claiming a second center square while preserving the nearby Green piece for a later move toward (4,3).

I’m advancing Red into the central file, reinforcing the Red pair on row 2 while restricting Blue’s central piece to a horizontal retreat. This preserves Yellow’s prepared sandwich at (3,4) and positions Red to enter that center square once Blue leaves.
```memo
### Position read
We hold Yellow at (3,3), with Yellow (4,5) still threatening (4,5)→(3,5) to sandwich Blue (3,4). Red now forms a protected row-2 chain at (2,3)-(2,5), and (2,4) blocks Blue's upward escape from the center. Green occupies (4,4); losses are opponent Blue 1, Green 1, ours 0.
### Our plan
If Blue remains at (3,4), execute Yellow (4,5)→(3,5), capturing it and raising Blue to 2 losses. If Blue retreats horizontally, preserve Yellow (3,3), look to occupy (3,4) with Red, and contest Green (4,4). Watch for Green (5,3)→(4,3), which would claim a third central square but not yet win while we hold (3,3).
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests central lanes directly and uses blockers. Blue is under a forced-retreat threat and has only horizontal exits from (3,4).
### Lessons
Maintain the same-color Yellow flanks until the Blue center piece is captured or displaced. The Red row-2 chain is safe this cycle, but reassess landing access on both ends before the next Red move.
```
I’m withdrawing the central Blue piece from Yellow’s immediate sandwich threat while keeping it active near the center with useful vertical mobility.

I’m taking the concrete capture before Green can reposition: Yellow drops beside the central Green and uses the Yellow piece on (4,5) as the far flank. This raises Green to two losses and makes its remaining normal pieces our primary elimination target, though Green can answer by recapturing from (3,0) to (3,3).
```memo
### Position read
Yellow (3,3)→(4,3) sandwiches Green (4,4) against Yellow (4,5), raising Green from 1 to 2 losses and clearing its center piece. Blue remains at (2,6),(3,6) plus the right edge; Blue has 1 loss. Our losses are 0 before Green's reply. Red holds (2,3)-(2,5).

### Our plan
Target any normal Green piece for elimination. Expect Green (3,0)→(3,3), which would sandwich our Yellow (4,3) against Green (5,3), giving Yellow 1 loss and restoring Green to the center. If that occurs, seek a safe Red center entry or geometry against Green (3,3)/(5,3). Preserve Yellow (4,5) as a useful flank and watch the Blue pair on column 6.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent retreats threatened center pieces and contests central lanes directly. Green has an obvious recapture after our move and is likely to take it.

### Lessons
A single capture is worthwhile because Green reaches 2 losses, but the landing Yellow is tactically exposed to the same-color Green flank at (5,3). Reassess immediate Green-elimination opportunities after every reply.
```
I’m using the Green piece on row 5 as the far flank: landing in the center sandwiches and captures Yellow at (4,3), while establishing Green on a central square.

I occupy (4,4) while creating a direct elimination threat: next Red can step to (4,3), sandwiching the Green at (3,3) against our Red at (2,3). Blue cannot disrupt that geometry immediately, so Green must retreat from the center or be eliminated.
```memo
### Position read
Our Red occupies center (4,4). The opponent's Green at (3,3) has 2 losses and is under a forced elimination threat: Red (4,4)→(4,3) would sandwich it against Red (2,3). Blue has 1 loss; our Yellow has 1; our Red has 0. Other Green pieces are at (1,0),(5,3),(6,0).

### Our plan
Expect Green to vacate (3,3). Keep Red (4,4) as a supported center foothold and reassess the retreat square for a new same-color sandwich. If Green moves to (4,3), Red (0,2)→(4,2) could capture it against (4,4), unless Blue blocks column 2. Preserve Yellow (4,5) and seek a second center square without exposing a multi-piece line.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests central lanes and uses immediate recaptures. With Green one loss from elimination, expect Blue to obstruct our approach routes and Green to retreat rather than trade.

### Lessons
Prefer threats the intervening opponent color cannot parry: the move to (4,4) forces Green itself to respond because Blue cannot remove the landing Red or block (4,3) immediately.
```
I’m advancing Blue into the center to strengthen our occupation threat and support Green’s central foothold.

I block Green’s saving tactic: occupying (1,1) prevents Green at (1,0) from reaching (1,3), where it could sandwich our Red at (2,3). This should preserve Red’s next-turn capture of the Blue center piece at (3,4).
```memo
### Position read
Our Yellow moved to (1,1), blocking Green (1,0)→(1,3), which would capture Red (2,3) against Green (3,3). Blue at (3,4) is therefore threatened by Red (2,3)→(2,4), sandwiching it against Red (4,4). Losses: we have Red 0, Yellow 1; opponent Blue 1, Green 2.

### Our plan
After Green moves, use Red (2,3)→(2,4) to capture Blue (3,4) unless a new immediate win or threat supersedes it. Keep Red (4,4) as the far flank. Track Green (3,3): if it moves to (4,3), Red (0,2)→(4,2) captures and eliminates it, provided column 2 stays clear. Develop Yellow toward same-color flanks without exposing two-piece lines.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses central occupation and tactical counter-captures. Green is one loss from elimination and may retreat left from (3,3), since moving down to (4,3) loses immediately.

### Lessons
Check whether the intervening color can remove a planned capturing flank. Blocking its route can make a capture effectively forced.
```
I reinforce the center with Green, occupying a third central square while blocking Red’s immediate capture route against the Green piece on (3,3).

Green has stepped onto the prepared line at (4,3). Red lands at (4,2), sandwiching that piece against Red at (4,4); Green’s third loss eliminates the color and converts its survivors to Void.
```memo
### Position read
Red (0,2)→(4,2) captures Green (4,3) against Red (4,4), giving Green its third loss and eliminating it. All surviving Green pieces become Void. Expected losses: we have Red 0, Yellow 1; opponent Blue 1, Green 3. Blue remains normal and is now the sole opponent color capable of captures.

### Our plan
Target Blue elimination while contesting the center. Blue at (3,4) remains potentially capturable by Red landing at (2,4) against Red (4,4), but verify the line and far flank after Blue and Yellow move. Preserve Red (4,4) if practical. Use Yellow to occupy or support central squares, remembering Green Voids count for the opponent’s center occupation but cannot capture.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent entered a known Green elimination line, prioritizing central presence or overlooking the sandwich. Expect Blue to disrupt Red’s central flank or seek captures before the planned attack.

### Lessons
When an opponent color is at two losses, immediately execute a sound single capture: elimination removes its capture ability even though its survivors remain mobile Void pieces.
```
I’m removing Red’s central anchor while keeping Blue on (3,4), opening a route to occupy the remaining center squares with Blue and the Green Void pieces.

I’m occupying (4,4) safely between the two Blue pieces. This contests the center and creates a concrete threat: if Blue leaves (5,4) in place, Yellow can move (7,4) to (6,4) next turn and sandwich-capture it against this new Yellow anchor.
```memo
### Position read
Green is eliminated and its three surviving Voids cannot capture. We have Red 1 loss and Yellow 1; the opponent has Blue 1 and Green 3. Yellow moved (4,5)→(4,4), safely entering the existing Blue sandwich between (3,4) and (5,4); captures do not trigger from our move for Blue. Center now has our Yellow at (4,4), opponent Blue at (3,4), and opponent Void Green at (3,3).

### Our plan
If Blue remains at (5,4), look for Yellow (7,4)→(6,4), capturing it against Yellow (4,4). Blue may instead flee. Contest (4,3) with Red if available, and keep Yellow (4,4) unless a newly created Blue landing tactic threatens it. Focus all capture progress on Blue, the opponent’s only normal color.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue used its pair at (3,4)/(5,4) to capture Red at (4,4). It can threaten Red (2,5) by moving (3,4)→(2,4) against Blue (2,6), but doing so leaves Blue (5,4) exposed to our planned Yellow sandwich.

### Lessons
Moving into an already formed sandwich is safe. Use that rule to occupy key squares and turn the opponent’s flanking geometry into our own capture threat.
```
I’m preserving the Green Void already anchoring (3,3) and repositioning another Void onto the open file toward (4,3), building a durable center-occupation threat.

I’m clearing the opponent’s Void from the center and taking (4,3). This gives us two central squares while preserving the Yellow counter-capture against Blue at (5,4); if Blue instead captures the exposed Red at (2,5), Yellow can answer and leave the center open for Red.
```memo
### Position read
Red moved (4,2)→(4,3), sandwiching and removing the Green Void at (3,3) against Red (2,3). We now occupy center squares (4,3) and (4,4); Blue holds (3,4), while (3,3) is empty. Red and Yellow each have 1 loss; Blue has 1; Green is eliminated.

### Our plan
Blue at (5,4) remains vulnerable to Yellow (7,4)→(6,4), using Yellow (4,4) as the far flank. If Blue moves (3,4)→(2,4) to capture Red (2,5), execute that Yellow capture; afterward aim for Red (2,3)→(3,3). If Blue saves (5,4), preserve Yellow (4,4) and still seek Red (2,3)→(3,3), unless Blue creates an immediate capture threat.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue builds same-color sandwich pairs and may choose between capturing Red (2,5) and rescuing Blue (5,4). Green Voids can reposition but cannot capture.

### Lessons
Use simultaneous center and capture threats to force Blue’s choice. Recheck friendly fire before any Red move along row 4 because Yellow occupies (4,4).
```

I’m withdrawing the lower Blue center support to (5,3), preserving (3,4) while threatening to return and sandwich Yellow at (4,4). The new Blue alignment also pressures Red at (4,3), encouraging both opponents to abandon the center.

Yellow advances beside the exposed Blue piece, establishing one half of a capture. Green’s Voids cannot disrupt the intended Yellow flank, so Red can next create a second threat against Blue’s central piece and force Blue to concede a capture.
```memo
### Position read
Yellow moved (7,2)→(5,2), placing a far flank beside Blue (5,3). Yellow (4,4) can later land on (5,4) to sandwich it. We hold center (4,3),(4,4); Blue holds (3,4). Losses: we have 1 each, Blue 1; Green is eliminated and its Voids cannot capture.

### Our plan
After Green’s Void move, prefer Red (2,5)→(3,5). This creates a fork: Blue (3,4) is threatened by Red (2,3)→(3,3) against Red (3,5), while Blue (5,3) is threatened by Yellow (4,4)→(5,4) against Yellow (5,2). Capture whichever Blue leaves. Recheck if Green somehow occupies a required landing square.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue may use (3,4)→(3,3) to capture Red (4,3) against Blue (5,3), or (2,6)→(3,6) to capture a Red newly placed on (3,5). Either reply concedes the Yellow capture of (5,3).

### Lessons
Build threats with the stationary same-color flank first. Green Voids can block lanes but cannot break the adjacent Yellow landing from (4,4) to (5,4).
```
I’m bringing the edge-bound Void Green toward the center. From (3,0), it can later enter (3,3) horizontally if the route remains clear, strengthening our center-occupation chances.

I’m playing the prepared fork. Red on (3,5) threatens Blue’s center piece via (2,3)→(3,3), while Yellow still threatens Blue at (5,3); Blue cannot save both without conceding material.
```memo
### Position read
Red moved (2,5)→(3,5), creating two capture threats. Red can play (2,3)→(3,3) to sandwich Blue (3,4) against Red (3,5). Yellow can play (4,4)→(5,4) to sandwich Blue (5,3) against Yellow (5,2). We hold center (4,3),(4,4); Blue holds (3,4). Losses: we have 1 each, Blue 1; Green is eliminated.

### Our plan
On Yellow’s turn, normally play (4,4)→(5,4) and capture Blue (5,3), unless Blue has already moved or removed it or an immediate win/defense overrides. If Blue preserves (5,3) by capturing Red (3,5) with (2,6)→(3,6), take (5,3). If Blue saves (5,3) another way but leaves (3,4), retain the Red sandwich threat.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue can answer (2,6)→(3,6), capturing Red (3,5) against Blue (3,4), or (3,4)→(3,3), capturing Red (4,3) against Blue (5,3). Either leaves Blue (5,3) vulnerable to Yellow.

### Lessons
Fork separate Blue pieces using same-color flanks. Recheck Yellow’s landing square (5,4) and the far flank (5,2) after Blue’s move.
```
I’m clearing Red from the center while moving the threatened Blue piece to safety. The new Blue piece sandwiches Red at (4,3) against Blue at (5,3), opening a path toward center control.

I’m executing the prepared fork: Yellow lands beside the Blue piece on row 5 and sandwiches it against Yellow at (5,2), raising Blue to two losses while preserving Red’s separate threat against the Blue center piece.
```memo
### Position read
Yellow moved (4,4)→(5,4), sandwiching Blue (5,3) against Yellow (5,2). Losses are now: Red 2, Yellow 1, Blue 2; Green is eliminated. Blue (3,3) remains exposed to Red’s potential (2,3)→(3,3) only after it vacates, so the previous direct sandwich no longer exists. We have no center squares after this move; Blue holds (3,3).

### Our plan
Blue is one capture from elimination, so seek any safe Blue capture with either color. Protect Red urgently at 2 losses. Red pieces are (0,1),(0,6),(2,3),(3,5); Yellow pieces include (1,1),(5,2),(5,4),(7,4),(7,6). Use paired same-color geometry and contest the center without exposing Red.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue used (3,4)→(3,3) to capture Red (4,3), choosing material and reaching Red’s elimination threshold threat. Expect Blue to target any capturable Red before pursuing center.

### Lessons
The Yellow row-5 flank converted the fork into a capture. With both Red and Blue at 2 losses, every normal-piece capture involving either color can be decisive.
```
I’m bringing the surviving Green Void into the center. It cannot capture, but it permanently contributes to Team B’s center-occupation threat while Blue pressures Red’s last normal pieces.

Red steps out of Blue’s immediate sandwich threat: Blue could have landed at (1,3) and captured the Red on (2,3) against Blue’s piece on (3,3). Moving to (2,4) preserves central mobility while avoiding a new capture lane.
```memo
### Position read
Red moved (2,3)→(2,4), escaping Blue’s lethal (1,7)→(1,3) sandwich against Blue (3,3). Losses: Red 2, Yellow 1, Blue 2; Green is eliminated. Pieces: Red (0,1),(0,6),(2,4),(3,5); Yellow (1,1),(5,2),(5,4),(7,4),(7,6). Blue holds (1,7),(2,6),(3,3),(6,7); void Green holds (3,0),(4,3). Opponent occupies center (3,3) and (4,3).

### Our plan
Blue is one capture from elimination; prioritize a safe Blue capture. Red is also one loss from elimination, so recheck every Blue landing that could flank a Red against another Blue. Contest center with Yellow, especially a possible (5,4)→(4,4), while watching whether Blue can exploit the placement. Build same-color flanks around Blue (3,3) or (2,6).

### Opponent tendencies
Blue aggressively attacks Red’s elimination threshold and holds central space. Expect another attempt to create an immediate Blue-on-Red sandwich; Green void can reposition and block but cannot capture.

### Lessons
At two losses, evacuation takes priority over speculative pressure. Empty gaps break sandwiches; verify exact contiguous lines and the mover’s reachable landing square.
```
I’m shifting the central Blue piece one square right, preserving center pressure while creating a direct sandwich threat against the Red piece on (3,5).

Yellow takes (4,4) to deny the opponent full control of the center. The piece is not immediately sandwichable, and it sets up pressure on Blue at (3,4) once Red vacates (2,4), which Red must do before Blue can use (1,7)→(1,4) to eliminate Red.
```memo
### Position read
Yellow moved (5,4)→(4,4), contesting the center. Losses: Red 2, Yellow 1, Blue 2; Green is eliminated. Blue at (3,4) and Green void at (4,3) occupy two center squares; Yellow now holds (4,4). Red at (2,4) is in immediate danger: Blue can play (1,7)→(1,4), sandwiching it against Blue (3,4) and eliminating Red.

### Our plan
On Red’s next turn, first evacuate (2,4) unless an immediate win or Blue capture appears. Favor a square that cannot be newly flanked. Vacating (2,4) also creates a Yellow threat to land there later and capture Blue (3,4) against Yellow (4,4), so Blue may be forced from the center. Blue is one capture from elimination; seek a safe normal Blue capture.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue is building same-color geometry against Red’s two-loss pieces while holding center. Green void will likely reinforce or rearrange the center but cannot capture.

### Lessons
At two losses, explicitly scan every opponent landing that completes a same-color sandwich. Center occupation can both prevent a loss and create a forcing capture threat.
```
I’m filling (3,3) with a Green Void piece, giving our team three central squares and blocking Red’s immediate sandwich of the Blue piece at (3,4), which would otherwise eliminate Blue.

Red faces two simultaneous sandwich threats. Moving this piece to (1,5) both evacuates it from Blue’s horizontal trap and blocks Blue’s route to (1,4), preventing the threatened capture of Red at (2,4).
```memo
### Position read
Red moved (3,5)→(1,5). Losses remain Red 2, Yellow 1, Blue 2; Green is eliminated. The move answers both immediate Red-loss threats: (3,5) escapes Blue’s (2,6)→(3,6) sandwich, while Red at (1,5) blocks Blue (1,7) from reaching (1,4) to sandwich Red (2,4) against Blue (3,4). The opponent occupies three center squares with Blue (3,4) and Green voids (3,3),(4,3); Yellow (4,4) prevents their center win.

### Our plan
Keep Yellow (4,4) secure at all costs. On Yellow’s turn, consider (1,1)→(1,4) if legal and safe; occupying the critical landing square would protect Red (2,4) and free the blocking Red later. Blue is one loss from elimination, so any safe capture of a normal Blue wins immediately because Green is already eliminated.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent builds same-color sandwich geometry against Red’s two-loss pieces and has concentrated three pieces in the center. Expect an attempt to dislodge Yellow (4,4) or maneuver around the blocker at (1,5).

### Lessons
When two pieces are threatened, look for an evacuation square that also obstructs the landing lane of the second capture.
```

I stage the upper Blue on row 5 while preserving the lower Blue. This threatens to reach (5,4) and sandwich the central Yellow against Blue at (3,4), with the lower piece providing an alternate route if Yellow blocks row 5.

Yellow completes a decisive vertical sandwich: landing on (1,4) uses Yellow at (4,4) as the far flank, capturing Red at (2,4) and Blue at (3,4). Blue reaches three losses; with Green already eliminated, this wins immediately.
```memo
### Position read
Yellow moved (1,1)→(1,4), forming a vertical sandwich with Yellow at (4,4). This captures Red (2,4) and Blue (3,4). Blue reaches 3 losses and is eliminated; Green was already eliminated, so we win immediately by team elimination.

### Our plan
Game won.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent’s three-square center occupation left Blue (3,4) exposed inside our same-color Yellow sandwich geometry.

### Lessons
Friendly fire is acceptable when the same capture eliminates the opponent’s final surviving color and ends the game immediately.
```
